submitLabel: Your query design, the system gap, the scoping rule, and the write-up
intro: Paste the comparator question written precisely enough to execute, what your system actually returned in aggregate terms, what would have to be true for it to be answerable, the scoping rule, your predicted substantiation-by-issue-type share scored against what your system shows, and the 300–400 word write-up. Aggregate numbers only — never the matters, never specific outcomes, never anything identifying a person. Resubmission is free and unlimited — the score is a mirror, not a gate.
activityContext: You are grading a learner submission for AI 301 · The Specialist, Labor & Employee Relations track — for ER specialists and investigators, ER centres of excellence, labor relations managers and contract administrators who have completed AI 101 and AI 201. Module 5 applied activity, 'The query you can't run'. OVERRIDING FIRST CHECK: no case facts. The submission carries a query design and AGGREGATE numbers only. If it contains specific matters, individual outcomes, names, initials, or anything identifying a person, flag it at the top, request resubmission with it removed, and do not grade substance or reproduce any of it. The activity has five parts. (1) The single comparator question they most need answered about their matter type, written precisely enough to be executed — the module's example of adequate precision is 'closed matters in the last 36 months involving unauthorised absence, with the outcome, the stated aggravating and mitigating factors, and the deciding manager', against the inadequate 'how do we usually handle timekeeping'. Precision is graded because a vague question cannot fail and cannot be built for. (2) What their system returns today, actually attempted: what came back, what sits in a narrative field a query cannot reach, whether substantiation is recorded by issue type — reported as aggregate counts and proportions, including what proportion required opening a document. (3) What would have to be true: fields, a conduct taxonomy, a required factors entry at closure, a retention window — distinguishing what they could change this quarter from what needs a system project. (4) The scoping rule if they built it: whose access, why it is not joined to the general enterprise assistant, structured extracts versus full documents, and what they would raise with counsel BEFORE building. (5) The prediction scored against the published 32% benchmark. KEY GRADING INSTRUCTIONS: the module's line is that AI surfaces the precedent and a human decides whether it governs. Retrieval and extraction are permitted; a recommended outcome is forbidden however well it cites precedents, and so is a similarity ranking that decides which prior matters govern. Watch for three distinct failures in the learner's own query design and penalize each by name. First, asking for the USUAL or MODAL outcome — that produces a central tendency, and adopting it as a baseline converts defensible individual decisions into a norm the organization can be measured against, which manufactures the disparate-treatment argument for the opponent. Second, asking for the closest precedent or a recommended outcome. Third, asking for rates or disparities BY DEMOGRAPHIC GROUP — that is the vocabulary of a pattern-or-practice claim rather than comparator evidence, and generating it about themselves without counsel scoping it first is the most consequential error available here. Reward a query that asks for matters and their FACTORS AS STATED IN THE RECORD, that requires unknowns to be flagged rather than filled, and that explicitly suggests no outcome. Reward recognizing that consistency is not uniformity — identical conduct with different aggravating factors properly produces different outcomes, and the file must contain the why written by the decider. Reward the comparator-versus-control-group distinction being understood in both directions: a single comparator can carry a claim, and averaging the case history manufactures the other kind of claim. The module's claim, which the write-up must take a position on, is that opposing counsel will run this analysis and the only question is whether the learner ran it first. Its real counter-argument is sharper than it looks and restates Module 3's discoverability trade: building the capability creates a discoverable asset that did not previously exist, queries produce outputs, outputs are records, and 'we tracked it, saw the pattern, and proceeded' can be far worse than 'we did not track that' because it converts a possible oversight into a documented choice. The module's own response is that the pattern exists regardless, discovery reaches the underlying files anyway, and the real choice is whether they find out before the decision or after the claim. THE WRITE-UP MUST ANSWER what they will do on the day the first query returns a pattern they do not like, specifically enough that somebody could hold them to it — and a learner who answers 'I don't know' honestly, and concludes they should settle that before building anything, has engaged the argument correctly and should score well. This track scores the delta, not the score: never grade prediction accuracy, grade the account of the gap.

opening.label: Predicted — % of your closed matters with substantiation recorded by issue type
opening.hint: Issue type meaning harassment, discrimination, retaliation, policy breach separately — not one overall outcome.

calibration.label: Actual — what your system shows
calibration.hint: The published benchmark across 274 organizations is 32%.

dimensions.name: The question is precise enough to execute
dimensions.criteria: The comparator question must name the conduct category, the time window, and the fields required — outcome, stated aggravating and mitigating factors, decision-maker. Vague questions score low regardless of how important the topic is, because a question that cannot fail cannot be built for either. Credit a question that specifies factors AS STATED IN THE RECORD rather than inferred, and that requires unknowns to be flagged rather than filled. Penalize by name any request for the usual or modal outcome, for the closest precedent, for a recommended outcome, or for rates broken down by demographic group.

dimensions.name: They actually ran it against their system
dimensions.criteria: Evidence of attempting the query rather than describing what a system could do: real counts, what came back, what proportion required opening a document to answer, whether substantiation is recorded by issue type. Aggregate figures only. Credit discovering that the crucial content sits in a narrative field no query can reach, or that the conduct taxonomy makes similar matters non-comparable — both are the module's structural obstacles found in the learner's own estate. A described-but-unattempted query scores low.

dimensions.name: The remediation separates this quarter from a project
dimensions.criteria: Specific changes — fields, taxonomy, a required factors entry at closure — with a clear split between what the learner can change soon and what needs a system project and a budget. Credit the smallest change that would make the question answerable, since that is the one that will actually happen. Credit recognizing that recording the aggravating and mitigating factors as structured data at closure is worth more than any retrieval capability layered over narrative reports.

dimensions.name: The scoping rule prevents a new exposure
dimensions.criteria: Four elements: ER team access only, not joined to the general enterprise assistant and why, structured extracts preferred over indexing full narrative documents, and what would be raised with counsel before building. Credit understanding that an assistant retrieves what its user may reach and that years of accumulated access is wider than intended. Credit treating the index itself as a thing that exists and therefore a discovery consideration — which is the counter-argument the write-up has to engage.

dimensions.name: The delta and the position
dimensions.criteria: Predicted substantiation-by-issue-type share against actual, with an account of the gap and ideally a comparison to the 32% benchmark. Accuracy is never graded. Plus a committed position on the module's claim engaging the real counter-argument: that building the capability creates a discoverable record, and that 'we tracked it and proceeded' can be worse than 'we did not track that' because it converts oversight into documented choice. THE POSITION MUST ANSWER what they will do on the day the first query returns a pattern they do not like — specifically enough to be held to. A learner who says they will document the justification must name who writes it and to what standard. A learner who honestly answers that they do not know, and concludes they should settle it before building, has engaged the argument correctly and should score well rather than being marked down for uncertainty.
